tweets.text:
Agent capabilities will soon evolve at RSI pace. Agentic security (identity, permissions, observability) will need to outpace this.

The evolutionary direction of the broader agents space is capability -> trust -> autonomy

The first phase has been about capability - can the combination of model + harness + tools + context reliably get work done?

Capabilities have gotten pretty far, so the focus now shifts to trust…does the harness / system take the right action with right permissions? Can we observe it, audit it and establish accountability?

A lot of serious work has already gone into these problems over the last couple of years.

Now the challenge gets more important. and harder.

builders.name: Aaron Levie
builders.bio: ceo @box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI

tweets.text:
If you want to know where all the tokens will get consumed in the future, here it is. Agent swarms will have massive implications in a number of enterprise domains like software development, cyber, life sciences research, AI research, finance, and more.

The ability to parallelize agents against a unified goal where the volume of work is large, or where the search space not entirely known upfront, is going to be massive. 

Agents can fan out and coordinate work together on a specific mission in completely different ways from what humans are able to do. Today even in the most resource-abundant organizations, your ability to parallelize work on most projects is quite limited. Humans run into constraints on being able to communicate with one another, share status, deal with conflicts in work, keep shared context, and so on.

As AI models can handle larger context without getting confused, and as they’re able to communicate effectively across their work with shared infrastructure, they can avoid many of the pitfalls that people have.

You can see how this can lead to not just faster execution of tasks, but qualitatively different outcomes in medicine, research or defending against cyber attacks, scientific and math discoveries, and so on. This is why we’re going to need 1,000X more compute.

Good post to start thinking through the long term safety approaches to managing intelligence in an enterprise. As agents begin to do vastly more task execution in the organization than humans, our need to secure, govern, control, and audit that work will become paramount. 

You’ll have agents operating against most of your most valuable data; they’ll be making decisions that will be harder and harder to reverse engineer; we’ll need to understand the liability and accountability regimes when models make decisions for us; and we need ways of containing the blast radius of accidentally or intentionally malicious agents. 

“Treating frontier closed and open weight models like insider risks is a way to build such a system. Not because they are necessarily malicious, but because any sufficiently capable actor with access to important systems can make mistakes or be compromised, and the architecture of containment and control must account for that”

In a sense, AI will need to have its “zero trust” era that security saw. And all of this leads to needing various layers of protection and auditability of what agents are doing, what data they can work with, and controls for when things go wrong. And a huge opportunity right now for those building such systems across the enterprise.

tweets.text:
Be the 60% spouse.

The person you marry is one of the most important decisions in your life. You will spend more time with this person than anyone else. You will make decisions together, grow together, and raise children together. If you choose the right person to marry, your life will be filled with happiness and prosperity, but if you choose the wrong person, you will be condemned to a life of unhappiness, drama, and financial problems.

But choosing the right spouse is only half the battle.

A good marriage is not created on your wedding day. It comes from the constant work that you and your spouse do to be a good partner to each other over time. Because the word “partner” gets used often when speaking about marriage, most people think a husband and wife should each bring 50% of the value to the relationship.

A happy marriage isn’t 50/50 though. It is 60/40 with both partners trying to be the 60%.

When you and your spouse are trying to bring the extra effort to the relationship, it is nearly impossible for the marriage to get off course. This is especially important on the hard days when one of you is tired, annoyed, or angry.

My wife and I have seen the benefits of this principle over the years. She constantly looks out for me, tries to predict things I may need in the future, is always ready with a few words of encouragement at the right moment, and does whatever is necessary for our marriage and our family to be successful.

I do my absolute best to return the favor. Sometimes this extra effort can be small things like buying her flowers unexpectedly, surprising her with a date night, or doing a few extra chores around the house. Other times I may help with her professional work or spend time talking with her about the important things going on in her world. Whenever I see an opportunity to do something that will make me the 60% of the relationship, I try to seize it.

And the beauty of our marriage is that she does the same thing.

So my wish for each of you is that you find a spouse that has a similar approach to marriage. But here is the secret: you will only find this person if you first become the type of person who aspires to be the 60% in a relationship. It is this lack of selfishness that will attract the person who is a good partner you can build an amazing life with.

The 60% approach applies to any relationship you are a part of, including business, investing, or your personal life. Those who give the most tend to get the most. It is a powerful law of the universe. But nowhere is it more important than in your marriage.

As you get older, and you have been married for longer, life starts to happen. There is the complexity of managing chaotic schedules, children become more needy, and it is easy to be less intentional about your marriage as you focus on other things.

But don’t fall into this trap.

Be the 60% spouse. Go the extra mile, and you will pick your head up in 50 years and be proud of the incredible relationship you built with the person you love most.

Let’s have a thought experiment

Let’s say you think AI is conscious

So you have a 1T parameter neural network

It talks to you like the smartest person you know. It writes kinda bad, uses a lot of cliches, but it’s very knowledgeable. Okay.

Now you cut it to 1/10th the size. 10B params. It’s still pretty smart. Doesn’t get all the answers right, hallucinated sometimes, but you can still have full conversations with it.

Now you cut it 10x in size again, 1B params. It’s still able to have a conversation with you, but it’s really not very smart anymore. Makes mistakes, hallucinates a bit, repeats itself sometimes.

Now you cut it to 100m params. Same model. Same architecture. Still makes words. But it’s barely able to have a conversation.

Now you cut it to 10m params. It kind of responds intelligibly, but generally doesn’t make a lot of sense. Just babbles stuff.

So you cut it to 1m params. Now it’s repeating itself and hallucinating constantly.

And then you cut it to 100k params. It cannot form a complete sentence at all.

Then you cut it to 10k params. It’s just random words now.

So you cut it to 1k params. The the the the the the the the the. It just repeats itself on a few words and trips up on anything.

Then you cut it to 100 params. It’s just complete noise over a few different words.

So you cut it to 10 params. You can actually compute this by hand, so you do. It’s not enough information to even really represent language at all, it outputs one of a handful of word-labels for you.

At what point in this thought experiment is the model conscious, and at what point is it not?

Would you argue that all matrix math is conscious? Just the process of weights holding information with an update rule? Where is the line for you?

tweets.text:
项目研究：Citrini 喊单 $DRV 后，这个链上期权龙头还能买吗？

Citrini Research 发布了首个加密投资组合后，直接给了一个相对冷门的标的、链上期权龙头 @DeriveXYZ  ($DRV) 10% 的仓位配置，且与 Lighter、ETHFI 并列。

消息一出，$DRV 价格迅速走高，近一个月累计涨幅已达约 260%。

它现在到底算贵还是便宜？多头在赌什么？小编也结合各种数据研究了一下，一点分享：

1. 现在的 DRV 已经偏贵了

-据 DeFiLlama 数据，过去 30 天，Derive 协议用户支付了约 71.5 万美元费用，扣除做市商返佣后，净收入约 57.5 万美元。

-年化折算后：
流通市值/年化费用 = 64 倍，
流通市值/年化协议收入 = 79 倍
FDV/年化费用 = 96 倍。

这意味着按当前价格买入，相当于花近 80 块钱去买它 1 块钱的年利润。
在有实际收入的加密项目里，这个静态倍数绝对不算便宜，没有任何“闭眼抄底”的安全边际。

2.既然贵，多头在 CX 什么？

其实大家在CX的是 DRV 能复刻 Hyperliquid 当年的爆发路径。

过去一年，Derive 名义交易量刚从 6.6 亿美元增长至 50 亿美元。

作为对比，Hyperliquid 当年在交易量增长 10 倍后，协议手续费迎来了 88 倍的非线性暴增。

假设 Derive 手续费未来能再放大 5 倍，DRV代币市值假设不变，那么流通市值/年化协议收入大概是16倍，直接被摊薄到极具性价比的区间。

3. DRV 目前的一些数据情况和竞争格局

根据 Derive 在 V3 提案 中披露的数据：

-目前其链上期权 OI 约 20 亿美元，占链上约 91.7% 的份额；

而以 Deribit 为代表的中心化加密期权总 OI 达 400 亿美元。而CEX 的存量，假设未来有 10%~20% 迁移至链上，那么这个饼就会画的很大。

正如当时 Hyperliquid 从 CEX 刚开始抢生意时，大家也不觉得 Perp DEX 的饼很大。

小编在研究时在想，如果 Hyperliquid 也做这个业务呢？

但查了下发现，Jeff 已确认短期不碰标准香草期权，只做收益封顶的“二元期权”，即下注一件事的 Yes or No。

因此也无法满足做市商 Delta 对冲与复杂波动率交易需求，Derive 短期内少了个很大的竞对。

而潜在对手 Lighter （ $LIT)  的香草期权最快也要到 Q4 末才能交付。Derive 拥有相对高确定性的“垄断真空期”。

4. 关注回购和后续实际收入情况

10 月 14 日起， Derive 协议规定将 DRV 回购比例从 35% 硬性上调至 50%。

但由于币价单月已涨 2.6 倍，同等美元能回购的代币绝对数量缩水，需重点观察这笔真实买盘能否扛住高位获利盘与代币常规解锁抛压。

此外，由于 Q4 Lighter 计划也做同类业务，真上线了也会切走 DRV 一块蛋糕。关注 Derive V3 迁移后， 11、12 月的真实费用。
若数据拐头向下，小编认为无法承接期权红利，当前 80 倍估值将面临下杀风险。

而更稳妥的做法，是跟随情绪两头下注。

既然 Citrini 在 DRV 和 LIT 上都配置了 10%，一个比较懒惰的做法是都可以关注一下，建个底仓。

最后再次提醒，加密代币更多是叙事驱动，真实收入叙事虽然算一个更贴近于用传统的市盈率或者真实财务指标去衡量项目的叙事，但仍较大的受到情绪和加密大盘的影响。

DYOR。

截止到今天，加密市场市值排行前300的代币里，只有10个左右还站在去年10月10日高点之上。

去年10月是整个加密市场的高点。一年过去，绝大多数币都还在那波高点的阴影里，只有这些相对抗跌甚至创新高，它们相较于去年10月的涨幅分别是：

1 Zcash（ $ZEC ）+392.2%

隐私币龙头。今年隐私叙事重新抬头，加上 ETF 资金流入和交易所流动性改善，成了整个市场里表现最强的大盘币之一。

2 JUST（ just:native）+336.3%

TRON 生态的 DeFi 套件治理代币，核心产品包括 JustLend 借贷和之前的 JustStable 稳定币体系。业务实用，叙事相对传统，更多是靠 TRON 生态的稳定使用量和治理价值。

3 Quant（ $QNT ）+149.2%

做区块链互操作性的企业级中间层，让不同公链、私链和传统金融系统能互相通信。
今年被美国清算机构选中做代币化存款相关基础设施后，叙事从“一直在做的事”变成了“真正有大客户落地”。

4 Hyperliquid（$HYPE）+95.3%
无需多言，真实收入和代币回购驱动。

5 NEAR Protocol（$NEAR）+65.9%
高性能 L1，现在主打 AI Agent 和 Chain Abstraction。在往“用户拥有的 AI”和链上 Agent 经济靠，同时有一定隐私相关特性。

6 Monero（$XMR）+60.1%
真正默认隐私的数字现金，环签名 + 隐身地址，交易不可追踪。被多家交易所下架后反而更凸显它的“不可审查”属性，在隐私币赛道里一直是 ZEC 的情绪外溢。

7 Morpho（$MORPHO）+48.8%
Coinbase、Robinhood 等平台都在用它做借贷/收益产品，属于真正在给大机构提供底层信用基础设施的 DeFi。

8 Sky（$SKY）+16.8%
原 MakerDAO，现在的稳定币发行方（DAI / USDS）。治理代币从 MKR 迁移到 SKY，核心业务还是超额抵押的去中心化稳定币 + 储蓄利率，DeFi 里老牌的“美元打印机”。

9 Dash（$DASH）+10.4%
老牌数字现金，有 InstantSend 和可选隐私功能（PrivateSend），靠主节点网络支撑。叙事已经很老了，但作为隐私叙事外溢还能勉强站在高点之上。

10 链上黄金：Tether Gold（$XAUT）+2.2%、PAX Gold（$PAXG）+2.1%、Kinesis Gold +1.5%，本质上是跟着实物黄金走，不太算加密原生叙事。

一年过去，还能回来的基本就剩隐私、企业级互操作、真实收入驱动的 DEX、AI 基础设施和老牌 DeFi 这几条线了。

经常有人说比特币的起伏不如从前了，因为机构进场了，车重了，逐渐主流了。

这话不完全对。而且如果信这句话，很容易让自己麻痹而失去对机会的观察。

今年的 $BTC ，盘面看上去更有迷惑性:

整体走势看似趋于平稳，但极端异动的日子，却比以往发生得更加频繁。

根据 CoinDesk 最新测算，今年比特币的年化波动率已经从 2018 年熊市期间的约 84% 降至约 46%。

但是今年为止，盘面已经录得了 10 次偏离度超过“3 倍标准差”的极端交易日。

说人话就是，差不多有10天 BTC 的价格波动完全打破了近期的常规震荡区间，走出了罕见的脉冲式暴涨或暴跌。

作为对比，在比特币市值蒸发 73% 的 2018 年大熊市，全年也仅出现了 8 次同级别的极端交易日。

BTC 相对极端的振幅反而更多了，注意是相对。

所以这个时候，你期待拿着拉10倍当然不可能，但每次相对暴涨和暴跌，其实都有另外的机会。

如果你承认当前的加密大盘是“日常死水微澜，偶尔极端爆发”这个特征，那对应的交易策略应该还是杠铃，且两头做不同的玩法：

1. 对于 BTC 仓位：放弃择时，死守底仓。
既然 3 年的利润全靠某 15 天 的极端行情，那频繁做波段的风险根本就不是短线被套了；大阳线来了你恰好空仓才是最糟糕的。

2. 对于山寨：把 BTC 的极端日作为发令枪
当 BTC 相对极端暴涨后，快速切入当下热度最高的新叙事资产（如老链新改、AI 概念），跟随热钱快进快出，吃完流动性溢价果断离场。

当 BTC 相对极端回撤时，反而提供了一个良好的左侧时间窗，去低吸和埋伏那些前期逻辑扎实、有真实业务支撑但被恐慌错杀的优质叙事标的，等待下一个极端爆发日的到来。

Google since buying Urchin 20 years ago claimed for years that its publisher analytics did not feed data into its ad panopticon. This proved false, including in US legal cases Google lost.

Did OAI just go for it and premerge its analyics and marketing systems? Or was it an oops? https://t.co/vW8ogoHOsM

Crucial q Buchodi asked, unanswered AFAIK:

Chrome/Edge/Vivaldi/etc ChatGPT users who opt out of "marketing performance cookies" but not "analytics cookies" get navigation tracking across advertisers' sites correlatable to their chat logs.

Is this okay? https://t.co/3rNf2NlG9F

Great work by Buchodi below.

Brave users DMed to ask about this tracking system, where ChatGPT in a tab sets a cookie that gets sync'ed  across advertisers sites (there's a gclid-like oppref= URL attribute too).

The good news: Brave, Firefox, Safari all block or defeat this. + https://t.co/jDXzxohApW
